props.text: ALSAP Overview

Asset Level Safety Assessment Plan

Understanding Astellas' approach to proactive safety surveillance

Welcome to this overview of ALSAP, Astellas' Asset Level Safety Assessment Plan. In this module, you'll learn what ALSAP is, why we're implementing it, and how it may connect to your work. This should take about 15 minutes. Let's get started.
The Challenge

items.title: Multiple trials run simultaneously
items.body: Multiple trials run simultaneously for the same drug candidate

items.title: Safety data accumulates
items.body: Safety data accumulates across these trials

items.title: Patterns can be missed
items.body: Without systematic review, patterns might be missed until late in development

props.text: Here's the situation: When we develop a new drug, we typically run multiple clinical trials at the same time. Each trial monitors safety carefully within its own protocol. But here's what we realized: safety data is accumulating across all these trials, and without a systematic way to look at the complete picture, we might miss important patterns until much later in development. ALSAP is our solution to that challenge.
Why ALSAP Changed Now

Over the past several years, the FDA has issued increasingly clear guidance on how sponsors are expected to manage emerging safety information.

One message is consistent across that guidance: safety signal evaluation is not optional, informal, or role-dependent—it is a sponsor responsibility.

That means regulators now expect companies like Astellas to demonstrate—not just state—that potential safety signals are identified, evaluated, escalated, and documented in a consistent, traceable way.
What is ALSAP?

items.title: 1. A Plan
items.body: A documented strategy for when and how we'll analyze aggregate safety data for a specific drug candidate (asset)

items.title: 2. A Team
items.body: Dedicated statistical programmers and statisticians who conduct these analyses

items.title: 3. A Process
items.body: A systematic approach that connects planning, execution, and decision-making

props.text: So what exactly is ALSAP? It's actually three things working together. First, it's a plan—a documented strategy that spells out when and how we'll look at aggregate safety data for each asset. Second, it's a team—we now have dedicated programmers and statisticians whose job is to conduct these analyses. And third, it's a process—standard procedures that connect the planning, execution, and decision-making. Together, these elements give us a proactive, systematic way to understand the safety profile of our drug candidates as data accumulates.

scenes.title: ALSAP Bridges Judgment and Defensible Process

props.text: From Judgment to Defensible Process

Historically, many safety-related decisions relied on expert judgment, informal consultation, and good intent.

While those elements remain essential, the FDA now expects those judgments to be supported by a clear, reviewable process—especially when decisions result in no action being taken.

ALSAP bridges that gap. It turns expert thinking into defensible evidence—showing how a conclusion was reached, who was involved, and why it was appropriate at the time.
ALSAP vs. Other Safety Processes

items.body:

props.text: You might be wondering: how does ALSAP fit with everything else we do for safety? Here's the key distinction. Trial-level monitoring happens in real-time within each study, often with blinded data. The Safety Management Team—or SMT—provides strategic oversight and makes governance decisions. The Safety Assessment Committee—SAC—steps in when we need unblinded review for regulatory decisions. ALSAP is different: it's the systematic, proactive analysis of aggregate data across trials. ALSAP provides the analytical foundation that feeds into SMT discussions and, when needed, SAC reviews. Each plays a distinct role in our overall safety strategy.

scenes.title: How ALSAP Works: The Basic Flow

props.text: The ALSAP Workflow

items.title: Step 1: Plan
items.body: Asset team determines ALSAP is needed → Drafts an ALSAP Plan (FORM-AST-34037)

items.title: Step 2: Assign
items.body: ALSAP programmer/statistician assigned to the asset

items.title: Step 3: Execute
items.body: ALSAP team extracts data, performs aggregate analyses per plan

items.title: Step 4: Review
items.body: SMT reviews ALSAP outputs → Assesses for safety signals

items.title: Step 5: Act
items.body: If findings warrant action: Document, escalate to SAC if needed, implement changes

props.text: Let's walk through how ALSAP actually works. First, the asset team determines that ALSAP is needed and drafts a plan that defines what analyses will be done and when. Second, an ALSAP programmer or statistician is assigned to execute that plan. Third, the ALSAP team extracts data from multiple trials and performs the aggregate analyses. Fourth, the SMT reviews those outputs and looks for safety signals. And fifth, if the findings warrant action—whether that's documenting the results, escalating to SAC for deeper review, or implementing protocol changes—the appropriate steps are taken. It's a systematic cycle designed to catch signals early.

scenes.title: When Might ALSAP Matter to You?

props.text: When Might ALSAP Affect Your Work?

You might be thinking: does this actually affect my work? The answer depends on your role. If you're in Clinical Operations, you might help coordinate data access for ALSAP analyses. If you're in Drug Safety, ALSAP findings could inform your signal detection work. Regulatory Affairs colleagues might use ALSAP outputs to support IND safety reports. Biostatistics and programming teams may collaborate on data specifications. And if you serve on a Safety Management Team, you'll be directly reviewing ALSAP outputs and making decisions. The key point: ALSAP isn't happening in isolation—it connects to many functions across the organization.

props.text: That completes our overview of ALSAP. To recap: ALSAP is our systematic approach to analyzing aggregate safety data across trials. It works alongside—not instead of—our existing safety processes. If you need more detailed information, key documents like the ALSAP SOP and plan template are available in our document management system. If you have questions about how ALSAP might affect your work, reach out to the contacts shown here. And if your role requires deeper knowledge—for example, if you're an ALSAP team member, SMT member, or Asset Lead—there are additional role-specific training modules available. Thank you for taking the time to learn about ALSAP.
